Evidence: ICE custody, judge's ruling, DHS outcry
#Aletheia #USPol

A federal judge's ruling to release an MS-13 fugitive due to prolonged detention without a bond hearing recklessly endangers public safety.

Judicial enforcement of due-process rights is reframed as reckless endangerment to fuel political narratives.

A federal judge ordered the release of an MS-13 member after ICE held him for five months without a bond hearing, sparking sharp criticism from immigration authorities.

Legal due process safeguards are weaponized into partisan wedge issues, obscuring the systemic failures of immigration detention logistics.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
Confusing procedural constitutional mechanics (WHO gets due process) with substantive moral endorsement of violent crime (WHAT happened).

Social Physics Analysis:
Officials run a smart selfish maneuver by using a high-profile criminal case to manufacture outrage against judicial oversight, projecting blame onto sanctuary policies while deflecting from detention delays.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Deception. The inversion of due-process protections into a manufactured crisis drives negative will.

The Unavoidable Truth: Constitutional due process applies even to dangerous foreign nationals in immigration custody.

The Unavoidable Lie: The judicial release was a deliberate endorsement of violent crime rather than a procedural remedy.
